correctness.rationale: Every pair of distinct deleted positions belongs to exactly one of the three disjoint classes by deleted-one count. Classifying the location of remaining zero and one runs proves T0=1+C(k,2), T1=1+(k-2)^2+ceil((k-2)/2) at a=3 or 1+(k-2)^2+(k-2) at a>=4, and T2=C(k-1,2)-1_{a=3}floor((k-3)/2). The exceptional identifications follow from equal zero-run lengths under rotation at a=3; they do not assume reversal equivalence. Algebra gives the two total polynomials. The embedded checker enumerates every two-position deletion event for 120 parameter pairs, using independent word-rotation and cyclic-run representations. This supports but does not establish the full infinite-domain proof.

value.rationale: Circular trace reconstruction naturally identifies rotations and must deduplicate distinct two-deletion outcomes. Exact support sizes are needed as finite-block benchmarks for circular observation and code confusability, yet counting them is obstructed by run-merging and multiple deletion events collapsing to the same necklace. The complete two-parameter composition-refined classification provides quadratic formulas and a sharp length-three-to-four run collision phase difference k-3; it is neither a renamed linear deletion ball nor a numeric table of unrelated parameters.
